findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed employees not using a barriers to shut off the faucet after handwashing. Education was carried out. The behavior was corrected. Endure that the appropriate procedures for handwashing are followed always to avoid recontaminating your hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The soda nozzles were observed with an accumulation of soil. PIC was made aware. PIC removed the soda nozzles and began cleaning them immediately. The nozzles were cleaned and inspected. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the nozzles of the soda machine are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following were observed.
1. The bins holding the lids for the single service cups on the right of the soda machine were observed to be soiled. PIC cleaned the bins. (COS)
2. The shelvings use to hold the bread trays and wrapping papers were observed with an accumulation of soil and dust. PIC was made aware. Ensure that the soil and dusts are cleaned to avoid possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed leaking/ponding water and a bit of rust in the bottom of the Prep cooler in the serving area. Discussed PIC and PIC assured inspector that the bottom of the prep cooler will be cleaned. Ensure that the ponding water and rust are cleaned appropriately.
findings.citation_text: 5-403.12 Other Liquid Wastes and Rainwater. Condensate drainage and other nonSEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following were observed;
1. Broken tiles were observed at the front of the back exit door to the facility.
2. An accumulation of food debris over the bread oven and the enclosed space behind the lids of the prep cooler. 
3. Soil and dust in other areas within the facility. 

Discussed with PIC. PIC assured inspector that the relevant actions will be taken. Ensure that these paces are cleaned properly and the relevant repairs be done for the tiles providing smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed dirty mop water siding in the mop bucket in the back. Inspector inquired about the mop water, employee told inspector that the water was from the night before. Education was carried out. The mope water was discarded. Ensure that the dirty mop water is always discarded after mopping at all times.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.15 Cleaning Maintenance Tools, Preventing Contamination. FOOD preparation sinks, HANDWASHING SINKS, and WAREWASHING EQUIPMENT may not be used for the cleaning of maintenance tools, the preparation or holding of maintenance materials, or the disposal of mop water and similar liquid wastes.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Inspector was unable to verify the food handling certification of the PIC. The other employee in the facility had a Food protection manager certification.  PIC told inspector that their certification had expired. PIC  assured inspector that they will get the training for the certification done. Ensure that the certification is acquired to be in compliance with the law. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the accumulation of soils on the surface of the ice dispenser on the soda machine. Discussed with PIC and the accumulated soil was cleaned to sight of touch while inspectors were on site. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.
